name: Remy Monroe
life: “I still remember earning a tip for directions I drew in dust.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Remy by a small Tuesday habit. Remy prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I stood by the turn and gave directions in three languages. My shift started without me.
appearance: Remy has a long face and high cheekbones. Look for a high puff tied with plain cord. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a dark green knitted vest with a little coil of soft measuring tape. In conversation Remy squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Remy has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To make the diversion directions work in three languages.
family: Casey Armas is Remy’s half-sibling. Remy is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Casey calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *A red mitten*, Casey says, “My sister and I disagreed about the color. Our mother called it tomato and settled a thirty-year argument.”
connections: Amos Tate. A lost ice sale and a morning spent translating become two claims on the same contractor.

reactions.situation: The diversion sign is only legible from close up
reactions.response: Remy reads the sign from the distance a driver really gets and reports the result.

reactions.response: Remy asks each person to say what they believe is actually owed before anybody proposes a payment.
